name: Ehud
title: The Left-Handed Judge
summary: Ehud was the second judge of Israel and a Benjaminite who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression. He is known for his bold assassination of the Moabite king Eglon and the subsequent victory over Moab, which gave Israel peace for eighty years.

keyEvents.title: Israel under Moabite rule
keyEvents.description: Because of Israel's sin, the Lord allowed King Eglon of Moab to oppress Israel for eighteen years, creating a need for a deliverer.

keyEvents.title: Ehud Raised Up as Deliverer
keyEvents.description: When the Israelites cried out to the Lord, he raised up Ehud, son of Gera, a Benjaminite who was left-handed, to deliver them.

keyEvents.title: The Hidden Sword
keyEvents.description: Ehud made a double-edged sword and fastened it on his right thigh under his clothes, hidden from the enemy as he went to bring tribute to King Eglon.

keyEvents.title: The Assassination of King Eglon
keyEvents.description: Ehud gained a private audience with the very fat King Eglon under the pretext of having a secret message, and killed him with his sword in his upper chamber.

keyEvents.title: Flight and Mobilization
keyEvents.description: After locking the doors and fleeing, Ehud gathered the Israelites in the hill country of Ephraim and led them to battle against the Moabites.

keyEvents.title: Victory over Moab
keyEvents.description: Israel struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all strong and brave men, and the land had peace for eighty years under Ehud's leadership.
